rules.statement: Authenticate CI workflows to cloud providers with GitHub OIDC role assumption rather than long-lived access keys stored as repository secrets, and trust the write/apply role only from a protected deployment environment while plan jobs use a separate read-only role.
rules.why: GitHub must hold no long-lived cloud credentials, so compromising a workflow outside the protected environment yields at most read-only access.
rules.check: Look for AWS access keys or similar static cloud credentials in workflow secrets/env, missing `id-token: write` with role assumption, apply roles whose trust policy is not restricted to the protected environment, or plan jobs using the write role.

rules.statement: Never run untrusted pull-request code with credentials: do not expose secrets to fork pull requests and do not use `pull_request_target` with a checkout of the pull-request head.
rules.why: A `tofu plan` from untrusted code can exfiltrate credentials through providers and data sources.
rules.check: Flag workflows triggered by `pull_request_target` that check out `github.event.pull_request.head` refs, or jobs that pass secrets/cloud roles to runs triggered by fork pull requests.

rules.statement: Never post OpenTofu/Terraform plans to pull requests or upload them unencrypted as CI artifacts or logs.
rules.why: Plan files contain secrets in plain text, and CI logs and artifacts on a public repository are public.
rules.check: Look for steps that comment plan output on PRs, `upload-artifact` of plan files without encryption, or `tofu show` of plans printed to logs.

rules.statement: Mark secret-bearing OpenTofu variables and outputs `sensitive = true`, and enable OpenTofu state and plan encryption.
rules.why: Values that are not marked sensitive, or state and plans that are not encrypted, end up published in logs or stored in readable form.
rules.check: Flag variables/outputs carrying tokens, keys or passwords without `sensitive = true`, and backend/terraform blocks lacking an `encryption` configuration covering both state and plan.

rules.statement: Keep vendor API tokens and operator-specific values (admin IP allowlists, contact details) in a secret store such as SSM Parameter Store SecureString, read at run time, never hard-coded in infrastructure code.
rules.why: Public infrastructure code must not reveal credentials or operator-specific details.
rules.check: Flag literal tokens, admin IP/CIDR allowlists, or personal contact values in .tf/.tfvars or workflow files instead of secret-store lookups.

rules.statement: Configuration that deploys the platform must consume reusable infrastructure modules and stacks only by a released tag, not by a branch, local path, or untagged commit.
rules.why: The platform runs the same released artifacts that are shipped.
rules.check: Look for module `source` references in live/cluster configuration that point to `main`, a branch, a relative path to the components, or no `ref` tag.

rules.statement: Give state-storage S3 buckets versioning, default encryption, a public-access block, and a TLS-only bucket policy, and use the S3 backend with native lockfile locking (`use_lockfile = true`).
rules.why: State needs locking and history and must not be exposed.
rules.check: Flag state bucket definitions missing versioning, server-side encryption, public access block, or an `aws:SecureTransport` deny policy, and S3 backends without `use_lockfile`.

rules.statement: Encrypt database backups on the client side before upload, and write them with write-only credentials to a separate bucket that has Object Lock in compliance mode.
rules.why: Backups contain signing keys and the Data Protection key ring, must be immutable, and must survive losing the database vendor.
rules.check: Flag backup jobs that upload unencrypted dumps, use credentials with read/delete permissions, or target buckets without Object Lock in COMPLIANCE mode.

rules.statement: Do not create IAM users or static access keys for automation; automation must use assumable roles with short-lived credentials.
rules.why: The dedicated cloud account permits no IAM users for automation, so no long-lived credentials exist.
rules.check: Flag `aws_iam_user` or `aws_iam_access_key` resources intended for CI or automation.

rules.statement: Pin the OpenTofu version in the infrastructure repository and in CI.
rules.why: Features such as `use_lockfile` and plan encryption need a recent OpenTofu, so the version must be pinned.
rules.check: Flag missing or loosened `required_version` constraints, or workflow setup steps installing an unpinned/latest OpenTofu.
